title: NDFIP2 Suppresses Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through DDX3X-Dependent R-Loop Remodeling and GNG13 Transcriptional Activation.
authors: Zhang, Enjian; Li, Yanfang; Shu, Jiaxin; Xu, Shang; Lv, Heng; Zhang, Chong; Zhang, Pengbo; Wu, Nai; Gong, Shuai; Zhang, Xiuzhong; Ren, Zeqiang; Zhang, Yi; Liu, Xin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究NDFIP2在结直肠癌转移中的作用机制，与cpcdh基因家族无关。
abstract: Distant metastasis remains the leading cause of colorectal cancer (CRC) mortality, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Integrating RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) profiling and clinical validation, we identified NDFIP2 as significantly downregulated in metastatic CRC. Functionally, NDFIP2 loss drove epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), stemness, and metastasis via PI3K/AKT hyperactivation. Mechanistically, NDFIP2 serves as an adaptor recruiting the E3 ligase NEDD4 to induce K48-linked polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of DDX3X. Unrestrained DDX3X resolves R-loops at the GNG13 promoter and recruits the transcription factor CTCF, synergistically enhancing GNG13 transcription to amplify PI3K/AKT signaling. Targeting this vulnerability, we engineered a cell-permeable NDFIP2-derived iRGD-conjugated peptide (ND-iRGD). In vivo administration of this construct suppressed DDX3X/GNG13/PI3K/AKT signaling, thereby attenuating distant metastasis and prolonging murine survival. Collectively, NDFIP2 acts as a critical metastasis suppressor via the DDX3X/R-loop/GNG13 axis, presenting the ND-iRGD peptide as a promising translatable therapeutic strategy for metastatic CRC.
abstract_zh: 远处转移仍是结直肠癌（colorectal cancer, CRC）死亡的主要原因，但其潜在的分子机制仍未完全阐明。通过整合RNA测序（RNA-seq）图谱分析和临床验证，我们发现NDFIP2在转移性CRC中显著下调。在功能上，NDFIP2缺失通过PI3K/AKT过度激活驱动上皮-间质转化（epithelial-mesenchymal transition, EMT）、干性和转移。在机制上，NDFIP2作为衔接蛋白招募E3连接酶NEDD4，诱导DDX3X的K48连接多泛素化和蛋白酶体降解。失控的DDX3X在GNG13启动子处解析R-loop并招募转录因子CTCF，协同增强GNG13转录以放大PI3K/AKT信号传导。针对这一脆弱性，我们设计了一种细胞可渗透的NDFIP2衍生iRGD偶联肽（ND-iRGD）。在体内给予该构建体可抑制DDX3X/GNG13/PI3K/AKT信号传导，从而减弱远处转移并延长小鼠生存期。总之，NDFIP2通过DDX3X/R-loop/GNG13轴作为关键的转移抑制因子，将ND-iRGD肽呈现为一种有前景的可转化治疗策略用于转移性CRC。
